title: Yes, finally! Shortcuts!
body:
Huge game-changer with the addition of the Shortcut actions. Most habits require only a simple press on the widget or on my watch, but a few of them, like adding time spent listening to audiobooks, require me to look at my BookPlayer widget and then move back and forth between the Habit app and the audiobook widget to enter the times.

My audiobook app only shows stats for the last 7 days and only provides them through its widget. If I don’t manually copy down the times every week, I completely lose the stats for those days.

Now, with the added actions for the Habit app, I can simply press an icon that runs a Shortcut I’ve built. It moves to the screen with the audiobook widget, takes a screenshot, extracts the data, parses it, and sends it directly into the habit tracker for me. This removes a TON of the tedious work!

This developer creates wonderful apps, but they’re often in desperate need of Shortcut actions. When they do have some, they’re usually pretty limited. So I was super excited to see this update!

Would love an action that could start the stopwatch/timer built into Habit! Pressing the Habit widget is ALMOST there, but it doesn’t actually start or stop the time itself. Same goes for the Live Activity; it takes you to the page but requires you to manually start the timer. This really isn’t a huge deal and doesn’t take any of the 5 stars away. Thought I’d just suggest it ;)

(The watch app could use the ability to start the timer as well!)

Thank you again for the actions! :D

title: So easy and powerful
body:
I have struggled with habits for almost all of my life. It seems like the only ones I can get constant, Aunt or my “bad” habits.

I’ve been using this habit tracker for a few months now. I track both my successes in improving, good habits, and my successes, increasing bad habits.

It’s easy to use, fun to use, and allows me to chart why I’m successful not just ticking a box to say that I am.

I have it on my phone so it sinks over my step tracker and my sleep tracker, then on my tablet at night when I’m reflecting on my day, I can document my successes in all areas of my habits, and provide myself a small amount of supplemental journaling.

I would highly recommend this application to anyone who is trying to improve their life by either increasing the positives or decreasing the negatives. It will help you in ways that you really don’t appreciate when you start.

title: Free use up to 6 habits
body: This app is great for the most part - you can add up to 6 habits under the free version which is fine for the most part, though I do wish that there could be more, and is the only reason I docked a star. I like that you can add a note for each completed habit and then see a page where all of the notes for that habit are shown in one place which makes tracking much easier. It has an optional feature that tracks how well you did for the day, so each completed habit adds more to a circle for that day so you can easily view what percentage of that day’s habits you completed which makes it feel like a game. It also shows you a bunch of different stats so you can easily view your progress in whatever way appeals best to you. The interface is very easy to use, looks really nice, and you can even customize the colors of different habits. I’d be happily willing to have ads on the free version if it meant being able to add more.

title: Did not like it and annoyed paying for subscription
body:
I paid for subscription (no free trial) and had to cancel it.  Despite many positive reviews I think it’s not a good app. It reminds you of vast variety of habits  you want to achieve, but super annoying with the reminders. Yes I want to drink more water, but I do not want reminder to pop up when I’m in the meeting. I do not drink water per exact schedule! 

Unless you are a control nut, where you do rings exactly at 10:35 or 1:52, it does not make sense. Plus it’s a whole lifestyle to track, so you get lost! I cannot pinpoint, but there is something about the advertising how it works and actually helping you—did not translate. 

Again I feel fools by paying it without ability to try. Next time I should remember to look for a free trial. I gut a yearly subscription (allready cancels next year)  and despite having a whole year to use it—going to delete the app, because it’s distracts and does not help. 

Pen and a small note book do better job.

title: I want to like this App
body:
First off there’s immediately a paywall/fee that should just be in the App Store rather than leverage the sunk cost fallacy of people downloading already. Ok so it’s $8 of at minimum $6. Not bad for a new ~notebook I guess, so I’m trying it. Developers need to pay for things too, so whatever. 

My problem: it doesn’t update values when I change my mind about the amount per day or month. I’m also not a big fan of non daily tasks showing up complete every day. For one, I find the value flaw extremely annoying. Please fix. Two: if I’m not doing something on a given day, I don’t want it showing up as complete just because I’ve done my month’s quota. I want to for instance track my period one day a month on a yearly basis. All I wanna see is the habit on the day I use it. Not everyday. Anyway, not an error but not my favorite method of tracking habits.

The count not changing nor updating is definitely a bug I’d prefer be fixed though, please. 

Thanks!

title: Please Read
body: Hello to anyone who can read my review or message right now. I hope you guys are having a good life/ day! I was going about this app happy and excited to finally find a way to stop my bad procrastination.. I struggle with going about life doing my daily tasks and chores of living. Waking up, going to work, coming home, doing my stuff, then repeating. (A small summary of a big life) I came across this app because a wise man once told me “Our habits, routines, and cycles dictate and change our lives.” So I can’t sit here doing the same things that hinder my growth because I don’t have a proper routine or tracker to help me. Hence this app and this whole Declaration of Independence I’m about to write up. I was getting into my creative mood and wanting to start my weekly schedule. What I do when I get home from work, chores, painting, anime, other things to make room and time for. But living life can be busy and I don’t make time when I should. I was in the process of adding my next habit using the “+” feature and I was stopped by a pop up of “Please buy subscription” to continue. Which we all know how that goes/ the face I made. 😐 Having it being set up as free from the start then changing without any warning was a surprise… But the offer of a free subscription for 3 days was nice. 👍🏻 So gotta make sure I cancel that so it doesn’t charge my card many times (If you know you know) ANYWAYS!  This app provides such a wide range of things to guide you along your journey. Tracks how you feel throughout your day, has a perfect set up for adding a new habit and all the in depth features of times, reminders, color, etc. Now I’m not hyping it up only 4 task in, but it has the proper organization I have been looking for in an app. ESPECIALLY one that gives me creative freedom.

title: Honest Review
body:
This app has been a game changer for me! Due to the designs displayed, I almost didn’t download the app because it appeared to be more “feminine”. However, I ignored that thought because the functionalities intrigued me (you can change the theme). 

I was looking for a way to track my commitments because many times I’ve lost sight of one or few of them due to how busy life gets. With this tracker, I’m able to set my own metrics for each habit and see the trends of my progress! Additionally, you can set a timer play audio such as forest sounds, and there is a sound for completion within a habit. You may also share your habits with friends. 

This method of tracking has worked better for me in comparison to tracking these habits as “tasks” in a to-do application. Being able to measure progress is great because it’s makes auditing yourself much easier and likely to be consistent. If you’re consistent with auditing your day-to-day habits, you will be consistent with those habits. This is perfect for staying aligned with your goals and values. 

Don’t hesitate on downloading this app. I was more than happy to pay for the lifetime membership; definitely worth the money.

title: Simple, customizable, easy to use, affordable
body:
Habits/Goals are easy to set up and edit just how you like. I love how simple and also intuitive the layout is. I also like that you can customize the tabs, interface, and what features you’d like to use, but it’s not too complicated to get it how you like. I love the dark mode, the widgets, the fact no account is required, and most importantly there is an affordable purchase option so no subscription is required!!!! I appreciate the Apple Watch integration as well!
FEATURE REQUEST: The only feature I’d like to see that I saw in another app, was a privacy minded way to have access to health data from Apple Health associated with a habit. You give separately read and/or write permission, and only to a specific health data variable like “Exercise minutes”. The app would then see when I have exercise minutes recorded in Apple health and check it off.. Also maybe access “mindfulness minutes “ for meditation. When you used a guided meditation app on iOS, it records “mindfulness minutes “ to Apple health. Then it would check off meditation. Or mark as minutes completed if you are setting time as a goal.

title: Perfect app, multi-device use is worthless
body:

This is a beautiful app but it is hamstrung by poor syncing issues between devices, and I am never on the same device for long. Syncing between devices works maybe 40% of the time and the developer has only ever asked if my cloud storage is full (it’s not). I strongly believe it is a bug. I’ve asked if there could be a sync button added to manually sync the data, but no dice. Swiping down, which is a common sync gesture, pulls up a filter for your habit data. I can’t disable and reenable cloud every single time I want to use this app

title: Lots of bugs
body:
Considering I paid $8.99 I thought the app would be extremely robust with no bugs. 
Some things I encountered in the first 20 minutes of using the app that I would like to be fixed: 
- the first time I added a custom habit it didn’t appear on the home page. I had to reload it by closing out of the app completely and reopening it.
- the slider intervals don’t adhere to the intervals I inputted in the “HabitBar Gesture” “add here” text entry box. In addition, the “x” to delete the pre-typed value is difficult to see, which is extra frustrating since you can’t delete the pre-typed value (of numbers with decimal values e.g. 0.02 hours) with the delete button on the keyboard. There is also no decimal point button on the keyboard so you can’t set the interval to non-whole numbers (e.g. 0.5 hours). Some more issues with the swipe right to check in feature but there’s just too many things wrong with it to list.

Some of the ui is a little confusing, such as the mood tracker being a modal only accessible by the small emoticon in the upper right corner of the home page.

I’ve only had the app for less than an hour trying to set up my habits, so I haven’t started actually tracking habits and been able to run into any bugs unrelated to setting up the habits. I do like how the app looks and works so I hope these issues can be fixed!

title: Not for Me
body:
I found it to be decent, but struggled to nail down a few customizations that other apps have a more smooth UX/UI for. Below are my four struggles with this app, plus two positives. 
Struggles: 
1. Reminders/notifications. I wanted to add reminders to specific days, while keeping the habits available for all days. For example, I may want to receive a reminder to workout on Tuesday, but if I don’t go until Wednesday, I still want to mark it off. Essentially, I don’t love how task days and reminders are linked. 
2. Tracking completion. I also find tracking completion to be a little more confusing than it needs to be. While adding an amount is helpful for some habits, there are times when I want to simply want to check a box with the more detailed options hidden away. Additionally, looking back to see what I’ve logged, in case I’ve already tracked the habit for the day, isn’t the easiest to discern. Yes, I can just check them off from the main page, but the simple interface should be fluid throughout, even with the custom options provided. 
3. Previous completion via the main page. I don’t love looking back at completion on previous days on the main page. Seeing a highlighted task is great to tell which I’ve completed, but seeing 2/3 of my goal for the week doesn’t show if I completed 2 on that day, or just 1 to add to my progress of 2 for the week. Again, other apps have figured this out better. 
4. Widgets. Great visually, but using them is less than helpful for how I complete habits (a max of 1 count tracked per day, per habit). I want to clic to track a single completion/count, and instead, it completes the entire goal when I click on it. Not ideal for me. 
Positives:
1. Customization. I do appreciate the amount of customization available. While I still find some areas where customization options are missing (reminder days), I overall appreciate the amount of customization available in other areas. They are typically just not to the extent I need, but I’m sure are great for some users. 
2. Pricing. The amount of access at the free plan is great, and even if you do decide to get the premium plan, the price is very affordable compared to others.

title: For people who want to build their own habit system
body:
This is a good app. It lets you start from scratch on whatever goals you are working towards and customize them in various ways. 

I like that the calendar shows the percentage of things you got done as I’m following a 80/20 goal of getting all my goals hit at least 80% of the time with a 20% grace for wiggle room. It’s been helpful in helping me keep up with my health goals in particular. 

I like that some of the pre-made goals you can add integrate with the Health app on iPhones so the app can also keep track of data from other health apps and a watch, if you have one. 

The design is also nice to look at, simple and colorful if you choose different colors for different goals. The widgets for the Home Screen are also useful to remind me to keep up my goals.

I got premium through a discount because I wanted to track more goals than the free version allowed, and the $8 lifetime fee I paid is already worth it. I think you can have maybe 5 or 6 goals for free.

And if I forget a day it looks at overall percentage… and if I actually did my habits but forgot to enter them that day, it lets me go back. title: Super helpful app! Some suggestions…
body:
Overall this has been versatile and a great way for me to develop healthy habits and track some activities for my kids. Connecting to my Health app has been nice for activity tracking. 

Things I find myself wanting that it doesn’t offer: 
— sub tasks/habits: I’m tracking when I eat and also things about how I eat. If I haven’t eaten yet, these habits don’t apply.
— A way to easily copy a custom habit as a template for others. I eat throughout the day and want to keep track of similar things each time. It’s been tedious to create the same habit repeatedly. I’ve tried increasing the count but don’t like not seeing each time that task was completed (the app just shows the most recent update on the goal status for that habit)
— Easier to review memos
— I’d like the Hide and Skip features to be a bit different. I don’t care about streaks, but I do want to know when I did/didn’t do a habit and easily differentiate from simply not tracking it for the day. I also want the calculations to be clear about the information they express. Higher percentage of days tracked isn’t the same as the percentage of days my habit was completed. Being able to show/hide or reorganize calculations would be nice as well. It’d make it easier to review the data I care most about. 
— Having an easy access to the time stamped view of completed habits for the day.
— I’d like to see my filters stay in place when I’m reviewing the status of my habits over various timeframes. (Ie last month compare to this month.)

title: Have to enter the app to mark done
body:
You can set up a habit to occur multiple times a day and set reminders for several times a day. This is good. However, to mark that you did it each time you have to open the app (tapping the reminder opens the app) then open the habit (tapping the plus on the habit does not mark it done) then in the habit tap the plus. Do not tap the check mark because that marks all instances done and if you subtract the later instances as done, the reminders will not notify you the rest of the day. Very cumbersome. 
Separate issue: The Apple Watch app extension gives you the notification, but if you tap it you get a msg saying there are no habits to mark done and to use the app on the iPhone to create some.
All and all a poorly designed product. I want my money back.

title: The app looks great, it fails in execution
body:
I was initially impressed with the clean and well-designed interface of the HABIT app—it’s visually appealing and exactly the kind of layout I like. However, my experience with its functionality has been disappointing.

I set up all my habits on my iPhone and expected a seamless synchronization with my iPad, but it simply doesn’t work. I reached out to customer support (which is only available via email), but their response was unclear. When I asked for further clarification, I was met with a dismissive reply: “I already explained in the previous email.” This level of support is unacceptable, especially for a paid app.

In summary, while the app looks great, it fails in execution—particularly if you need to sync between devices. I regret spending my money on it, and I strongly advise others to avoid it. Not worth it!

title: Look nice, but unusable
body:
I downloaded this app solely to check off days that I didn’t have a drink. The app seemed easy enough to navigate, but I ended up being so frustrated just trying to do this one thing. 

The habit/goal kept showing whenever I tapped on a calendar day, and I don’t know why I couldn’t just un-tap it. I went to the FAQ and it said I needed to go to the Habit Manager, but that was for removing the habit completely. I finally got it to take me to the page showing my weekly goal, which was showing as complete even though it wasn’t. I had to manually visit each day and use the reset option. 

After all of that, I ended up creating the habit from scratch to make sure I got the settings right, and the same thing happened again. I went ahead and uninstalled it after that. 

I’m fairly tech savvy and can usually work out new apps and interfaces without too much trouble. So, chalk it up to human error, but I don’t think it should be so confusing for an average person like me to check a box on a calendar.

title: Good for goal oriented people
body:
I’m a goal-oriented person who loves lists and checking things off, so this app is perfect for me.

Using it with my Apple Watch has made daily habits feel like a game. I don’t always have my phone on me, and I tend to ignore notifications, but with the watch, I stay on track and mark tasks off easily.

That said, the Apple Watch version has a small issue—I can’t enter amounts (e.g., logging 24 oz of water or a 30-minute workout). The option to add amounts is there, it just doesn’t work. I have to use my phone, which is mildly inconvenient.

I also wish there was an option for habits every two or three weeks, rather than specific days of the month. I’ve worked around it, but it would be a helpful feature.

title: Everything you need
body:
Some habit tracking apps are limited to daily goals and can create guilt from not finishing everything that day. This one does not do that.
You can make habits for daily, weekly, and monthly goals then build on them as you integrate it into your routine. You can also customize notifications for a specific goal as a daily reminder. I especially like seeing the weekly and monthly progress pages to compare the habits and see what I’m falling behind on. While the design may not be flashy, it has all the bells and whistles I need to help me accomplish my goals. I highly recommend!

title: GitHub-Style Year View is a Game Changer
body: The year-view is game changer. Unlike most habit apps that only show recent week, or at best a month, this app lets you see your entire year in one view. If you use GiHub, you know how motivating it is to see this scope of time. Tracking your habits over the course of a year is the appropriate scope because habits often don’t “kick-in” or matter for almost close to a year. Having a year-long target means you’re getting a realistic understanding of the effect of a habit and not just a short snapshot, which doesn’t inform you much about the story of long-term positive change. Habits are fully customizable with frequency, weekly targets, color, name, icon, reminders, duration, units to measure (minutes, hours, miles, kilometers). You can even create your own units! Want to do 100 backflips per day , three days per weeks between Monday - Friday at 11:30AM!? You can do that with this app! This app has, is, and will continue to change my life. Download it now!

body: I’m a 23 almost 24 year old woman who has looked for so many apps to help track my progress and habits that I want to incorporate into my day/week or life in general. You can edit pretty much everything to your liking, and when I downloaded it I had a deal to spend a couple dollars to get a chart that made it easier for me to track, the daily things get darker in color depending how many you completed (ex. I made my “drink 10 bottles of water/day” section blue, if I drink all 10 the little square will fill in the blue. If you drink none it stays white, drink some it’s a light blue) and the things you want to quit stay the color you chose if you had none of whatever it is and get darker in color the more you have. like I’m trying to quit drinking, if you exceed the limit that you set then it turns black. title: Not terrible but could be better
body:
Honestly, I wanted to love this app but I just don’t. I started using it to do a habit challenge with my family. 

Issue 1: Not the most intuitive app. It’s not terrible but it definitely takes a few minutes to get the hang of it. I ended up FaceTiming with my family to show them how to get it all setup. 

Issue 2: My mom (in her 60s but decent with technology) ended up buying the premium because it was confusing when you first login. If your fingers get click happy make sure you pay attention to what you’re pressing. 

Issue 3: I created group habits with my mom, dad, sister, BIL, and husband. Sometimes the habits glitch and don’t register people saying the accomplished the habit for the day. So it looks like they didn’t complete the goal/habit for the day on the group tab but on their tab is shows done. Normally that’s not a problem, but now I have to ask if they completed the habit. Additionally, if anyone makes a change to the goal then you have to resend the shared goal to everyone for it to register for anyone to track. Again, not a huge deal but still a pain in the butt. 

Issue 4: I don’t see a way to easily see who completed what habits on past days. I have to go into each habit and look at each habit (if the habit even registers as “done” see: issue 2). 

I even tried buying the “lifetime” account and it didn’t help. It was such a waste of money. 

Ultimately, the app has so much potential (and even offers the potential) but the execution of it is just subpar. If you’re only tracking your own goals, then this app is fine. Buuuut if you plan on trying to do the group function, which is why I got the app to begin with, I don’t recommend this app.

I have ADHD so I bought this app to make my life easier but this problem isn’t helping because when I don’t see the habits I forget about them. What do I do? 

Also why does it automatically fill in habits? 

I Also wanted to suggest for this app, along with tracking habits, to also have a todo list feature for the day. I think I, along with many other users, would love the simple addition of daily tasks along with habits. 

If they get all the bugs fixed then this app would be great

title: What a beautifully designed and thoughtful app

I came upon this app after wanting something to help me track habits on my phone. I’m a big fan of Atomic Habits (a book that I highly recommend) that is life changing and this app is the perfect tool for something like that. It is so customizable in colors, emojis, themes and that makes it more fun and visually appealing to use. It also has suggested habits to help if you get stuck. I used to write my habits in a planner or paper but found it was hard to keep up because I don’t carry a planner around with me everywhere I go as much as my phone. This app is so much more convenient and because it has everything I need and I come back and use it daily. That makes it for it to be an effective habit tracker and builder. Props to the development team for being so thoughtful on this app. Thank you!! 

The basic feature allows 5-6 free habits and the premium features allow more.  I’ve been using the free plan for a week and I’m in love with it and am considering upgrading. They are also one of the rare few to let you buy lifetime membership for one price which makes me think of the old days when apps first came out. title: My favorite app!
body:
God bless whoever created this masterpiece. This app is definitely worth the money. I love that it offers a one-time payment that you don’t have to worry about subscribing, and it’s a great price!

There’s so many positive things I could say about Habit Tracker. This is my second time purchasing the app on a new phone because I’ve loved it for so long. 

There’s 2 daily quotes with a custom background, a super-cute progress graph. You can use emojis or pre-made icons on each habit. Number of habits is unlimited and fully customizable with bright colors, times, and reminders. 
There’s a mood tracker with notes to briefly journal your day! It even comes with widgets to choose from! Not to mention the timer that’s available for any habit (such as meditating or reading.) 

I’ve tried multiple habit tracking apps and have never found one that compares. Habit Tracker is straight to the point, no annoying presentation slides to click through. No pressure from the app to complete tasks, or guilt tripping memos when you forget about the app. No unnecessary notifications. Extremely straightforward with customizable options all around. 

This is a non-negotiable need for anyone like me with ADHD or procrastinators in general. 
I will use this app for the rest of my life!

title: The widget is what one need to have their habit app working

I figured I need to overview my daily progress in a very convenient way so I keep stay on top of my habit list of all time. And to do that, widget would be the perfect place to do so without opening the app to stay on top. What I currently using is the list weekly view widget, it shows a full week of progress with a list of all my current habits. With it I am actually wanting to complete my daily habit because I continue seeing how much effort I have made and wanting to continue the progress which will helped me actually making real progress. This is my 5th day with this app and so far I complete 100% on all my habits daily and I was never able to achieve that with any other habit app over the year. Suggested this app 100% to anyone struggle following along with other habit app.

title: Best of ALL Habit Apps tried
body:
I like this app so much that it is the first app I ever purchased after a decade of using free apps. I’ve tried at least 10 different habit/productivity apps. Here’s why this is the best habit tracking app: (1) You can TRACK DIFFERENT COUNTS, such as frequency, minutes, or hours. You can also track by day or week and adjust when you want your week to start. Other apps don’t offer that variety. (2) This app is VISUALLY appealing, which makes it motivating for me to use the app to check off my habits. Other apps are so plain, what’s the motivation for me to use it? I could just go back to using my plain calendar. The visuals are my favorite feature since they are like a positive reinforcement for when I use the app (3) AFFORDABLE. It’s less than $10-20 bucks for lifetime which is a reasonable deal. I don’t think anything more than $10-20 is worth paying for when we haven’t experienced the app long enough to see success. Other apps charge like $50+ which is ridiculous! I also hate the subscription model. I want a one time payment. (4) You can TURN OFF REMINDERS. I hate reminders because my schedule varies daily. At 5 pm today, I might be at work, but at 5 pm tomorrow, I will be working out. Reminders don’t work for people like me who have variable work schedules-they are a nuisance. I want to track my habits by the week or month or year, not day. This app offers that ability. (5) The free feature allows you to track like 5 habits which is enough to tell if it’s effective. Other apps only let you input 1-3 habits which is lame. I’m trying to change my life here, and 1-3 habits isn’t enough as a trial. (6) simple interface and easy to use. I don’t want lengthy quizzes asking about my lifestyle before using the app. (7) customize your habits. We are all different! This app acknowledges we have specific, unique goals! Thank you for this app!

Trust me, I downloaded and tried 10+ apps to track my habits. This one is the best by far. It’s the only app I was willing to purchase in the past decade. Love it!

title: Hope improvements are made in the future
body:
As someone with ADHD I both thrive and rebel against a structured day… I love that hit of dopamine when I get to tick off something I accomplished/completed off my list…. But I also tend to get overwhelmed by analysis paralysis when I see a giant list of things I need to do. I have to break down tasks into lists of micro tasks or steps.

I like that I can create a “morning self care habit” and make it need 5 taps to complete, but I wish I could make habit clusters instead so I can see which tasks I struggled with. For example my Am Self care consists of washing my face, taking my vitamins/meds, oral care, remembering deodorant and doing something with my hair. On low energy days I may say eh to washing my face, or decide to leave my hair in a braid because I’m not leaving the house.

title: Love this App!!
body:
I’ve been using the Habit app for a couple of years now, and I absolutely LOVE it! I can’t live without it. The widget on my phone makes it so easy to track my habits at a glance. It’s been a game changer, helping me stay in control of my life and healthy habits. The app clearly shows what I need to improve on and what I’m doing well, and the reward system is a great motivator.

However, I have a suggestion for improvement. When I review my performance for each habit, whether I check off the habit or skip it, it shows as completed on the calendar for monthly and yearly review view points. This doesn’t give me a true view of my consistency. It would be great if the review and monthly overview could differentiate between completed and skipped habits. If this feature already exists in the settings, please let me know!

Additionally, while I know you can set habits for specific days or every day, a more flexible option would be nice. I’d love the ability to set habits to be done, say, three times a week without specifying the days. A floating check-off option that continues to pop up every day until I complete it would be perfect. Overall, the Habit app is fantastic, but these tweaks would make it even better!

title: Simple and effective
body:
As someone with ASD, it’s often hard for me to remember things such as to eat or especially to brush my teeth. I’ve tried all sorts of habit tracker apps in the past, and they’ve always ended up distracting me more than completing my goals (I’m not a fan of the ‘pet’ type trackers, they keep me on my phone when one of my goals is to stay off of it!)

Habit Tracker is a lovely simple design that isn’t overwhelming to look at, it provides reminders and a journal section— I honestly love it. It even gives me a streak on my habits! Each time I don’t feel like getting up to brush my teeth I always do because I don’t want my streak to reset after so long! It’s a really effective way to get me to stay on top of it without it seeming too childish.

The simple design is easy to navigate and sort through.

Overall, I have nothing negative to say at all! This is the one tracker app I’ve found that actually helps me!

I also want to give a shout out to some pretty amazing customer service. I Identified a bug in one of the report features and reached out, not expecting a response anytime soon. Instead, I heard back immediately, which was basically in the middle of the night, and they had the bug identified, fixed, and an update rolled out by the next morning. title: Nice app with a two flaws that kill it for me
body:
This app is so close to being amazing. I would use it as my main habit app, if it was not for two problems that are severe for how I want to use it, making the app unusable for me personally. 

1) When tracking time for a habit, if you accidentally add the wrong amount of time, there seems to be no way to undo it except to reset the timer for the full day. Thus, if you are not aware how much time you had already accumulated and then you make a mistake, you completely lose track of your tracked time for the days. This has happened to me so many times I've lost count.

2) When adding time to a time-tracking habit, if you don't perfectly hit the center of checkmark representing that some amount of time should be added, you instead return, and refrain from adding time. It is very easy to accidentally do this and think you have added the time when you have not. 

If the developers fixed these two issues I'd be very happy to return to the app.

However, creating custom habits is more difficult than it should be. On the iPhone, the keyboard hides the submit button and I can’t get it hide the keyboard (even after watching YouTube videos). 

Also, it sends HRV notifications I’m not sure are based in health fact. Even if they are, at no point should they use the alarming word, “terrible”. I’m a big proponent of HRV and know it’s useful. I have other, more accurate, devices to track HRV. I think it’s worth this app reconsidering if they should use HRV as a parameter. If they do, they should retitle some alerts.

Overall this is by far the best app of its version I have tried, with the customizability, simple interface, and accessible system. 
However, two pain points keep me from fully enjoying it: 1. It seems impossible to switch a habit between “build” and “quit” after it is initially created, which is frustrating when trying to figure out which suits a habit better. 2. Even after you have completed a habit for a day, if you have a notification set for a certain time it will still remind you to complete it, which is demotivating. It seems weird that reminders are not based on whether the habit still needs to be completed. 

If these two points are updated I will surely give the app a resounding 5/5 stars!

body: I’ve been using this habit tracker for years and finally paid for the app a few months ago. It’s a simple, decent app and seemed to serve my needs for a while. I convinced myself to take the app to seriously and kept on using it. However, recently I set a few habits to last a specific length of time. Several of those habits I completed 100%. (Example: I’m going to run three times a week for the next six weeks). I completed that example habit, completing those 3 runs, for 6 weeks straight. So why does my end result say my overall rate is 98%? Shouldn’t it be 100%? There are too many habit trackers out there for me to be stuck on this one. Heck, I might as well whip out Excel and figure it out from there.

title: Life Changing App
body:
This is the first app I’ve ever took the time to write a review on. 

Pros: 
- completely customized habits that you want to have or habits you are trying to break.
- can change the colors of each habit
- can schedule as often as you like reminders 
- can track weekly, monthly, and yearly progress 
- free version or they offer a paid version that’s worth the cost
- can change the sounds on reminders
-Home Screen widget features

I’ve been using the free version for about a year but it only allows you to have like 3 or 4 habits on there. So it wasn’t really worth looking at the app besides sending me daily reminders like read at certain times, go to the gym and get ready for bed. 

Then last week I discovered the widget feature where it shows my habits on my Home Screen. Now that I had a convenient way to see my habits daily, I paid the $8 for a lifetime membership which let me add 15 habits to my Home Screen. Now it’s a daily reminder to get those things done per day. It literally 10x my productivity and is worth every penny. I’m also a big checklist guy so that’s probably why I enjoy this app so much. 

My two mild inconveniences from this app is when I’m trying to create a habit. Sometimes the keyboard screen won’t go away after I’m done typing. The second one is that if I’m editing a habit and changing the reps or count (mins to hrs) or whatever, then it makes me lose all my old day’s data. I would rather it just keep my old data and just change the future “reps” to the new numbers. That way it shows that I was consistent before and still consistent with the new numbers. Other than that….. perfect habit tracking app!!!!

body:

THIS APP AINT LIKE THAT!! I'm Pavloving myself to make sure I keep up with eating hearty carbs and balancing out extra glucose-full and salt-filled snacks. Yo soy obligado to give review as I would like to support this app as much as possible! 

The free version is so well done. >>NO NASTY ANNOYING ADS<< !! The notification sounds are a bit annoying on principle, I'm picky with sounds, and I can't seem to figure out how to download new ones, but a good amount are pleasant enough that I can trick myself into blacking out every ~half hour and the next thing I know I've chugged a ton of water and eaten a super carb + salty/sugar filled snack! It has been helping me eat 3 meals a day plus snacking for my blood sugar/POTS, drinking 64+ OZ water, and reminding myself to stretch and get my joints to stop dislocating! I have hypermobile ehler's danhlos syndrome and partial/total amnesia. So an app being easy to navigate is BIG IMPORTANT! And reminding myself to be healthy-ish is so useful! 

TOO LONG DIDNT READ: APP LAYOUT IS GREAT FOR BAD MEMORY, app is fun! free version is flawless as is! THERE NO POPUPS OR ADS!!!! Only 5 habits to customize, but they are So customizable and easy to edit and navigate! Much obliged to  support fully as I hate most apps! LOVE AND DOWNLOAD!

title: Great app for tracking [paid version]
body:
Update: it seems the update fixed the crashing. However, I still believe there could be improvements for better quality. Still, the amount of customizations are so unique, it really creates a great looking app to actually WANT to open & complete. Even the features are great, for the price. I paid for it in full. However, if it turns into a subscription, I’d like the option of being “grandfathered” in. Some features I like.
👍
- timer for reading & optional sound.
- Full customization (colors, creation, day/week/month
- icons. Decent amount for each habit
- mass add. Especially great for retracking when updates mess the app up.
- stats option.
- share habits. I share with my wife & we know when we update. It’s awesome!
- option to turn off quotes & mood. I don’t care to see those, although others do.
So many more I could talk about.

Fix
• widget: tap works, but display doesn’t show it live, so I tap over & over, which messes up my count. I switched back to “open app” option.
• crash: it still crashes during certain customizations; changing colors, choosing icon, choosing small option of habits

Ideas
• bright colors = text contrast change. Too bright, you can’t see txt for intuitive mode, which looks better than simplified.
• PIC: Actual transparent / blur option for pics
• PIC: choosing what part of pic for widget.
• widget: color gradient background option.
• sound: I like the confetti, but have an option to turn off sound on completing each task, or maybe give an option to change the sound, like with timer for reading
• intuitive: gradient colors, choosing the options. Not a top, but a cool visual idea.

I’m excited for new updates to come, making it stable, but also for better features.

The widgets are perfect because they’re the first thing I see when I open my phone and they’re interactive so you don’t even need to remember to open the app.

title: Handy, minimalistic habit tracker
body:
Coming from Android, I was looking for an alternative to Habit Now. This app was exactly what I was looking for! 

I love the sort of “heat map” that gives a quick glance as to how I performed with my habits on any particular day, plus the general reports to see changes over time. 

But my favourite feature is the memos which I find are extremely useful for writing down notes related to the accomplishment of a habit on a given day. I love being able to look back to verify something I’ve done or didn’t do. 

Having the neat widget on screen also motivates me to keep track of my habits so it’s a win all around. 

Thanks so much for this great app!

And it has been incredibly successful. I personally really like the data return- having my percentage available resonates very well in my brain! 

I would like to suggest, however, a deeper breakdown capability of the data. In example, I would like to be able to see my percentage from smaller time frames. Ideally a timeframe I can determine. I would like to be able to choose from date to date what timeframe data I am looking at. That would help my process incredibly, as I use three weeks at a time to determine my “score”.

title: Adults with autism need this
body:
Having been diagnosed with autism has helped me understand so much more of my brain. Using lists helps me know exactly what I have done and what is next to do. Having it on my phones screen right away at a glance helps when I’m in or near meltdown mode. Even when I am freeze mide. Where my brain literally just stops because I am so overwhelmed with things to do I just freeze…. This app is able to help me to know what’s next. 
I hadn’t heard of this app until my psychiatrist and nutritionist told me about it. It really helps even with just the free version. Someday I hope to be able to buy the full version. For now having reminders to eat and ability to track if I’ve already eaten has helped alot. I can’t wait to be able to know if I have taken my meds, brushed my teeth, ran the washer (or more like switched the laundry because I always forget to do that!)

title: Simple and life changing, excellent design
body:
This app is flawless. I have tried many other habit, productivity, and checklist apps, and none compare to this. I use this app to keep track of all my daily habits, and it is a beautiful and pleasant experience. It allows complete customization of all habits - down to frequency, time of day, build vs quit, color and icons in the list, ect. In other apps I have tried, it can feel cumbersome to update the list or set them up properly.

I recently upgraded to the premium version after a long time of using the free version. The premium is very affordable, and now that my habits are more solidified, I was ready to upgrade for more features.

I’ve used this app for a long time, but with new commitment at the new year, this app has really allowed me to change my life in wonderful ways. Many thanks to the developers for making something so beautiful and useful for free!

title: Phenomenal App
body:
Like the title says, this app is phenomenal. It’s a great way to track progress on a habit you’re trying to get down. I’ve used it to develop a skincare routine, read more, exercise more consistently, and keep track of medications I’ve taken throughout the day. I find it incredibly satisfying to close a habit too. 

I also enjoy the app’s emphasis on stats. Each time you close the little habit bar, it adds to your current streak. They have stats readily available and a multitude of charts and graphs to keep up with your habits. And it’s easy to customize too. You can play with the app’s icon and colors, habit colors, in app colors and pretty much anything else in the app.

There’s a vacation mode too, where it’ll skip habits automatically within a timeframe you set. And there’s a bunch of features I’m sure I missed. The app can work with Apple’s health app and keep up with your steps for you to see if you’re meeting your goal, which is convenient if you track everything else in the app.

And the app tries to prevent cheating as much as possible. Like you can’t check off a future habit for instance. 

Would definitely recommend if you want to start some routines and need a way to keep up with your progress.

title: Fantastic app to track habits!!!
body:
Seriously the BEST habit tracker I found. All the other ones are “free” where they limit you to nothing except opening the app before they spam you with upgrading to a $9.99/month subscription. This app has an actual free version that’s very usable, and beyond that a lifetime purchase is only $5.99! Extremely fair and reasonable, and a price I was more than happy to pay for how polished, clean, and useful this app is!

The app itself is very clean and modern looking, as well as very easy to use. Lots of customisability, great graphs and insights and gorgeous widgets! My two favourite things are the yearly overview where I can see all my habits on one page and how many days out of the year I’ve completed them, and the second is the widgets so I can easily see which habit I still need to complete and I can easily tap it and mark it complete from my Home Screen.

Overall this app feels very polished and clean, works great and has really good detailed stats on you habits that make it a joy to log everyday and keep you motivated. That, along with a non-subscription model and a price of just $5.99 for lifetime access makes it one of my favourite and most used apps!

title: Please fix notification issue
body:
(12/15/23 Edit:) Brought it back to 3 stars since the issue is still not completely resolved. I really like this app but the notification issue is a big problem for me. See below for context. 
(12/14/23 Edit:) This is genuinely an amazing app. I honestly just need this app and the default iOS Reminders app and I am plenty organized with those two. This is the only app I've been happy with for reminders and habit tracking among the many others I've downloaded and deleted. I don't get this functionality with any other app and it comletely meets my picky ADHD needs. I used to own an Android and I had an app that I loved but it wasn't available for iPhone sadly. This app is the closest thing to it and satisfies those standards. The only thing I could think of that I wish they had is the ability to attach images. They're only improving this app with updates and they even just added a mood tracker which I might start using too. I paid for the premium version but it's completely worth it in my opinion and it's just a one time payment without subscription. (11/14/23:) This is an amazing app for habits and reminders. I really do think it deserves 5 stars but I can't even give it 4 stars for one big reason: almost anything you do will clear all of your habit notifications. I'll list below the ways your notifications can get cleared. I promise if this one issue gets fixed I'll change it to 5 stars. If I could just get persistent notifications from this app that DO NOT CLEAR ON THEIR OWN then I'll be 100% satisfied. 1. If you mark a Habit complete from a single notification, it will clear all of them unprompted. For example, say you have a Habit notification for cleaning and another Habit notification for reading on your lockscreen. If you mark the cleaning habit complete it will make the reading habit notification disappear along with any other Habit notification on your lockscreen leaving you with no notifications for the habits you haven't completed yet. 2. If you open a Habit by swiping, this also potentially clears all of your Habit notifications. 3. Even if you just open the app itself, all of your notifications can get cleared at the same time. I do not really use the widget so I'm not sure if that also causes notifications to clear but I wouldn't be surprised if that were the case. I could have missed other ways that triggers this action but these are all the possibilities I know of and can think of. Please fix this 🙏

title: Changed my life 🤩
body:
Fantastic app with simple but effective interface that helped me change my life by instituting important habits. The UX is great, especially the celebrations and design because it is so cute it makes me want to stick to my habits. The data collection and reporting is fantastic for looking back.

I do have a couple of suggestions-
I exported habit data because I needed to change the frequency of one of my habits from daily to every other day, and it told me it would be deleting all that habit’s data. Now my physical therapy routine suggests me going back to daily, so I wish to re import that data I backed up so that I can continue that habit again. I know I could have just paused the habit, but I truly didn’t think at the time that I was going to need to go back to it. I regret it, but at least I backed it up - could you guys make it so that I could reimport the data?

Also, amazing job with the customization of units and frequency for habits. I was just wondering if you guys could make an option for an every-X-days habit? E.g. if someone wanted a habit done every other day, they could workaround right now by selecting say all the even days in the month or 3 days of any week, but it gets a little wonky because not every month is 30 days etc. it’s a lower priority, but would be nice to have!

Also also - I have some friends that really want to try this app after I show it to them, but they are android users. Would you consider putting your app on like the Google Play store for them?

title: An amazing habit tracker!
body:
I’ve been using Habit since it was originally free and it has since then helped me keep track of what I needed to do in a day, consistently. The widgets and user interface are are both understandable. You can take a glance at the widgets and it will tell you all the habits that you have and haven't finished yet. I haven’t seen any other habit tracking app give the user this much customizability. You can change icons, descriptions of habits, what time Habit should notify you about a habit, make the habit timed or a count, and even make habits weekly. All of this customization comes with the free version, although I believe it only gives you 3 free habits to keep track of, unlike the premium version which gives users unlimited habits.
I consistently workout and do any weekly chores without forgetting because of Habit! Life can be overwhelming sometimes so having an app remind you of what you need to do can be handy. This app does motivate you to do your habits. The streak system, sound effects for completing a habit, and the mini calendar that gets marked with a completed habit, are all subtle celebrations that encourage the user to keep completing habits. 
Overall, Habit is a very user friendly habit tracking app with many customization options. It will ensure that you’re consistent with your habits!

If you do drink, you swipe the habit as you would in “habits to end.” When you do this, the habit stats show “complete” as opposed to “failed.” Not sure why.

Appreciate any feedback from the developers on this.

title: great app! I love it!!
body:
I downloaded Habit for habit/ task tracking. But I specifically downloaded it for a wellness assignment for my college class. I have goals for myself for being on top of my meals (and keeping them healthy) and sleeping a good amount of hours each night and also going to bed by a certain time! 

I love the user experience of the app for the most part overall and I especially like that you can put notes (memos) under each task too! Personally for example, I check off that I ate lunch and I put in the memo what I ate that day. Or for my sleep goal when I check it off I write the amount of hours I slept that night and for the bedtime I write the exact time I went to sleep!

I love the fact that I can put in the memos overall. And also the fun (and satisfying) sound for when you check off you completed the task for that day which definitely gives me a bit of a boost in my serotonin and I feel accomplished and proud of myself! 

For each task you create, you can put in the frequency (if you want to make sure you do the task at least X times per week) or you can pick which days you want or need to complete certain tasks e.g. my goal is to go to bed before 2am on non-class days and by 1am for my class days. You can also set reminders for yourself and choose the time of day overall or a specific time you would like it to remind you! You also have the option to change the sounds for the notification (and I believe the checking complete sound too— but that is a fact from memory). 

I gave it 4 stars because it took me a moment to figure out how to navigate things at first, but once I got it I loved it! I highly recommend this app to everyone and I’ve told all my friends about it too!

title: Interactive Widgets PLZ
body: PLZ add interactive widgets for adding water via widget. // I just got this app, and i’m already in love, the lovely minimalist icons you can choose, and the widgets. Very very good! Thank you for including dark mode, UI customizations, and custom icons, that is HUGE. The app is very customizable which I love. If a few small changes were made, the app would be absolutely perfect - This app’s main strengths are its Swiss style, very easy to read icons, and levels showing habits which are completed. The “Today” tab, and “Overall” for making habits seem to be the main usable features. The “Habit Tracker” tab near settings, detracts heavily from the app, i’m trying to be like a handwritten journal with script typography. [There are tons of confusing apps like this on the app store, and what makes this app unique is how simple and aesthetic it is, so the handwritten planner, with highlighter texture, and underlined areas randomly on that tab is very very confusing. Please design it like the other tabs :) - Please link specific widgets to specific habits [For example, a widget just for tracking water, when clicked on, please route this into the water tracking habit. Currently it opens to all habits, which creates extra steps to log water. - Ability to turn off hints [lightbulb icon] - Ability to link Spotify vs just apple music - Perhaps an option to show the total oz of water needed in the widget, or the current water daily % [an option to show this instead of the date?] - too easy to add water or subtract 1 oz, with the + and - symbols. Often I subtract some accidentally, and want to undo, but the only undo button is to reset the whole day - Saying “Complete” vs “Done” when editing a habit makes it seem like clicking the button will accidentally mark the habit as complete / fulfilled. - Perhaps changing the color of the icon can be in the same menu as the icon, to avoid going through two menus quickly and hitting “compete” each time

The premium cost is so cheap that it's certainly worth trying, just to gauge potential usefulness to you. I've been using this over the past few months during a period of mental health difficulty, and it has helped with implementing better habits and providing visual motivation. There are multiple widget options, with good customization ability. The "quit" habit feature is a favorite of mine, it's great for routines you want to stop doing, as you can set it to revolve and just forget about it, only needing to update the habit if you break the streak. I don't personally use the water tracking, but it works perfectly with Apple Health. It's somewhat rare to see an app that combines this level of functionality with a smooth UI and negligible price.

title: Wonderful app for people with disabilities
body:

 I’m able to be more independent instead of my family doing many things because I couldn’t remember. This app is allowing my family to worry less about me forgetting to drink water, eat, take my meds and chores around my home, etc. 

The basic is great but the premium allows for me making custom tasks and that would be a game changer. Thank you so much for this easy to use app. Thanks to this app, I am able to function much better than I have in years. I’ve tried similar apps but this one tops them. Additionally, they have mental check-ins which I find to be helpful in helping me to relax and calm down when I’m getting panicked.

title: Great app overall, but one really annoying thing
body:
So overall I actually love this app, and it’s helped me keep up some good habits I’ve been trying to build as well as some “don’t do this today” attempts to break bad habits. 
The only thing I don’t like is that after you mark off a habit, it keeps sending you reminders. So if I complete one of my weekly habits on Monday, I still get daily notifications to do it for the rest of the week. Same with monthly habits. There is no way to only send notifications once a week or once a month either. 
The reason this is a big deal is because it creates an overwhelming number of daily reminders and often for things I’ve already marked off, which makes me more likely to ignore the reminders for things I haven’t done yet.

title: My favorite tool for building new habits

I have had this app for over a year and I LOVE it!

There is a free version that gives you 5 habits. I started with those 5 just to test the app, but quickly realized the full version would be well worth the money spent. 
I can add as many habits as I’d like and they’re all customizable. You can change the color, icon, time of day, notifications for each habit, etc. These are easy to edit and organize. 
I especially love how I can see my stats for the day, week or month. This is great way to reflect on what habits are working, which one need more attention or which ones need to be changed.
Probably the best feature about this app is the customizable widget. Having my habits on my front home page make it easy to remember and record what I’ve completed. 
This tool would be perfect for anyone looking to track and build their habits.

title: Efficient and User-Friendly Habit Tracker: Perfect for iPhone Users
body:
I recently started using the Habit Tracker app on my iPhone, and it has proven to be an essential tool in helping me develop and maintain healthy habits. The app offers a simple yet effective interface, making it easy to track my progress and stay motivated.

One of the standout features of this app is its user-friendly design. The interface is clean, intuitive, and aesthetically pleasing. Navigating through the app is a breeze, and I was able to set up my habits and start tracking them within minutes of installation.

The app has built in habits and alls allows you to create custom habits based on your personal goals and preferences. Whether you want to establish a regular exercise routine, track your water intake, or develop a reading habit, the Habit Tracker app can accommodate your needs. It offers a wide range of pre-defined habit categories and also allows you to create your own custom habits, providing a high level of flexibility.

Tracking your habits is incredibly easy with this app. You can set daily, weekly, or monthly goals and mark off completed habits with just a tap. The app provides visual representations of your progress, including streaks and statistics, which is highly motivating. I found myself eagerly striving to maintain my streaks and achieve my goals, thanks to the app's intuitive tracking system.

Another notable feature is the reminder function. The app allows you to set reminders for each habit, ensuring that you don't forget to perform them. These reminders can be customized according to your preferred time and frequency. I found this especially useful for habits that require regular attention, such as taking medication or practicing mindfulness.

title: Good, but needs to be polished
body:
I have the premium version, and I think it’s well worth it. However, I have some suggestions because this app could use some polish.

First, when you add a note to a habit to appear under the habit name, the text is always white. Because of this, its either barely visible or invisible because the colors of uncompleted tasks are too light. Furthermore, the color of the text for the habit name is always black. So when you complete a task and the color darkens, it becomes much less visible.

What this means is that your “Today” page will often look like a mess. Some text stands out, some is invisible, and it all looks frankly unpolished and ugly. This is disappointing because this page is the one you use most.

Another problem is the “Habit Tracker” calendar page. Frankly, it looks bad. There’s no other way to say it. The 6 available “Report Styles” all look juvenile and cluttered. Everything on the calendar feels small and cramped, and scrolling from week to week is a chore because of those tiny arrow buttons. This could be fixed by simply getting rid of that big “Habit Tracker” label on the top, and shrinking the stats at the bottom.

I want to love this app, but I can’t. Not yet. I’ll keep using it for now, but unless the UI doesn’t improve, I will probably eventually leave. I really would prefer a sleeker, more minimalistic, more professional looking app. I hope you take these comments into consideration, because I really do like this product but it definitely needs some improvement.

title: This is literally the perfect app
body:
I came upon this app because I was looking for a way to keep track of taking my meds and brushing my teeth in the morning. This tracker has fit all of my needs and more. It’s simplistic and doesn’t overwhelm you with too many functions, like I’ve found from other apps. It lets you skip your tasks without any guilt tripping or forcing, which is a function unique to this app honestly. 
It also is ad free and generally very unobtrusive. While it does have a premium function, you are never bombarded with reminders about it, and none of the necessary functions are locked behind a pay wall. If you do decide to get the premium, it is extremely cheap and adds a few very nice extra bonus features. 
This app is now the reason that I never forget to take my meds or brush my teeth, it also helps me keep track of how often I do certain tasks such as showers. 
Generally it is a 10/10 app and I really do recommend it

title: Pretty good, stats could be improved
body:
I’m on lifetime membership. Feedback:

1. Don’t count days that haven’t happened yet as “zero”

Habit stats are always presented in terms of the total window of time you’re looking at.

It is Tuesday and I had a perfect day on Monday, but it tells me that I’ve met “19%” of my Habits this week (in red text, which I assume is coincidental). 

This is true for any window of time. There’s one more week of April, so on the monthly view of one of my habits (which I’ve been perfect on), it shows “80%.”  Yearly view “11.51%.” 

I understand the argument that I’m “19% of the way toward completing all of my habits this week,” but you should distinguish more clearly between that and “You have not completed 81% of the habits you intended to.” 

2. Let me add extra minutes and seconds at the same time when I put more time toward a habit than my minimum requirement — better yet, let me put in my total (if above my minimum) all at once 

If my habit minimum is “10 minutes per day” and I do 20 minutes and 34 seconds, I currently need to: state that I did my minimum 10mins, add an additional 10 minutes, click save, add an additional 34 seconds, click save.

I should be allowed to, at minimum, enter the total minutes and seconds I went over and then save (add my 10 mins, then add the total I went over at once: 10m 34s). But ideally if I know I did 20m34s today, just let me say that from the get. 

3: On the individual habit page, indicate that you need to scroll side to side if you have more than 5 habits

This took me awhile to figure out and was frustrating while I got used to the app

4: Make it more obvious where I need to go to edit my habit 

Scrolling to the bottom of the individual habit screen is not intuitive 

5: Give a more readable view of memos 

It’s very unlikely that I’ll ever think “Which Yoga class did I do on March 2nd?” I will instead think “What was the name of that upper body yoga class I did last month”

title: An effective and motivating habit tracker
body: I've been using this app for a few months now, and I have to say, it's made a huge difference in my life. The app is incredibly user-friendly, with a simple and clean interface that makes it easy to track my habits and stay on top of my goals. What I love most about this app is the level of customization it offers. I can set up reminders for each habit, choose specific days of the week to focus on certain habits, and even track my progress over time with graphs and charts. The app also has a wide range of pre-set habits to choose from, which is great if you're looking for inspiration or just starting out on your habit-building journey. But perhaps the best feature of this app is the sense of accountability it provides. I love being able to see my progress and check off each habit as I complete it. It's incredibly motivating and has helped me to stay on track with my goals. Overall, I would highly recommend the app to anyone looking to build new habits and achieve their goals. It's an incredibly useful tool for staying organized, motivated, and on track.

title: Amazing
body:
I recently started using a time tracking app, and I must say it has completely revolutionized the way I work. This app has made it easy for me to keep track of how much time I spend on different tasks, which has helped me become more productive and efficient.

The app is incredibly user-friendly and intuitive, with a simple interface that is easy to navigate. It allows me to create different projects and tasks, and then track the time I spend on each one with just a few clicks. I can also set goals and deadlines for each project, which helps me stay on track and focused.

One of the features that I particularly appreciate about this app is the ability to generate detailed reports. I can quickly see how much time I have spent on each project and task, and even generate charts and graphs to help me analyze my productivity over time.

In addition, the app is also highly customizable, allowing me to tailor it to my specific needs. I can choose from a range of settings, including the option to track time automatically, manually, or with a timer.

Overall, I would highly recommend this time tracking app to anyone looking to become more productive and efficient in their work. It is an incredibly useful tool that has helped me manage my time more effectively and achieve my goals with greater ease.

title: Good, but needs some UX/UI improvements.
body: I was looking to update my process of completing daily tasks - I use standard Reminders on my iPhone, but I wanted to be able to track my task completion over time and see real-time data. Other reviews go into detail about how great this app is, and the range of data it can provide you, and I agree. I will also mention that the level of color customization and widgets is so much fun - I loved making it my own style as I was adding tasks! But the UX/UI feels like it was made for an iPhone 5. Instead of natural swiping motions (as many people use to read books on their phone, scroll Tiktok and Twitter), this app has specific, small areas of the screen that have to be tapped precisely to navigate parts of the app. Namely, on the 4th “tab” Calendar Icon of the habit tracker. I have to press the tiny arrows next to the week when I want to see week-by-week progress, but my thumb naturally wants to swipe to get there. It gets a bit frustrating to precisely tap my finger while holding my phone, and made me notice how useful apps that I can navigate one-handed are. (Also, this 4th tab is very middle-school graphic design vibes with the sun and moon. It’s cute, but it just looks old and dated on an iPhone 13. I would lean towards modernizing this.) Also, on the 1st “tab” with the plus sign, it would be useful to see upcoming tasks for tomorrow (similar to Reminders), because I sometimes have to do a task one-day early (laundry before going out of town, etc). That swiping motion for completion is super useful. Just need the ability to swipe between days here too!! A consistent existing button at the bottom of the app to add a habit would be good too - I personally don’t see much value in the 3rd Tab “Group” as I live alone. A button to quick-add a habit would be much more useful to me, but maybe that’s personal preference! I will continue to use, but I will be really, truly satisfied with my purchase if updates like the above come down the line.

title: Best habit app!!!
body:
I struggle with my mental health and doing daily easy tasks (brushing my teeth twice a day, washing my face twice a day, etc.)
I have used other habit apps before, but always found myself getting too overwhelmed because there were too many bells and whistles and it wasn't as simple as just checking off a task. This app is the perfect solution. I just add my task, and when I complete it, I click on the app and then just swipe right to say i'm done! and it makes a little noise! and if you complete all your tasks for the day, you get a little fanfare! i love that so much.

I also have a task for exercise, and it syncs with my apple watch / health so it automatically completes the task when I achieve my goal for the day which I love. 

The widgets are also well designed, and perfect to see what your progress is and serves as a good reminder.

I also really appreciate the development team on this app. If you want to purchase premium, they offer an option to request a discount which I think is so lovely for folks who may want premium but can't afford it. (As a suggestion, maybe include somewhere where folks can pay more than the premium amount to contribute to that donation fund? Not sure if y'all have that already, but just a thought!)

I love this app so much I purchased premium myself, and I literally never spend money on apps. I know this whole thing just sounds like an ad, but it really really isn't. For the first time in YEARS, I have consistently flossed my teeth for a month. It sounds like nothing, but for me, its huge. Incredibly thankful for this app, and cannot recommend it enough :")

title: Keep yourself on track!!
body:
I recently started using the Habit Tracker app on my iOS device and it has completely transformed the way I approach my daily habits. The app is simple to use and has a great user interface, which makes it easy to navigate and set up new habits.

One of my favorite features of this app is its flexibility. It allows me to track a wide variety of habits, from simple tasks like drinking more water and taking breaks at work, to more complex habits like reading a book or exercising regularly. I can easily customize the habits I want to track and set goals for how often I want to perform them.

The app also provides reminders, which is extremely helpful for keeping me on track. It sends notifications to remind me to complete my daily habits, and I can customize the frequency and timing of these reminders. I love how it keeps me accountable and ensures that I never forget to complete a habit.

Another great feature of this app is its tracking and reporting. The app tracks my progress on each habit and provides detailed reports on my daily, weekly, and monthly performance. I find this to be incredibly motivating, as it helps me stay motivated and focused on achieving my goals.

Overall, I highly recommend the Habit Tracker app for anyone who is looking for a simple and effective way to track and improve their daily habits. It has completely transformed the way I approach my daily routines and has helped me become more productive and focused on achieving my goals.

title: The only habit tracker that is working for me!
body:
I’ve tried other habit trackers, but this is the only one that is really helping me build better habits. It’s not overly complicated, very well made and functions very smoothly. 
I love that I can view my progress of the habits weekly, monthly, and yearly. My favorite feature is the visualization of habits yearly, because it is very thoughtfully designed. Each box represents a day, arranged in 7 rows (representing each day of the week) by 52 columns (representing each week of the year). This helps me visually see whether I’m actually making this year a year of better habits, while at the same time showing me how I’m doing each week. Being able to do habits together with friends is also very helpful. I’m also grateful that the lifetime premium features of this habit tracker is a one time fee that is very affordable. Thank you for making this wonderful app!

title: Excellent App and Just What I Need
body: What a great App! Everything I need is right in one place and it’s a great tool to help you build and keep habits. It’s not like one of those apps that gives you a hard time if you aren’t able to complete a habit one day. It’s a motivational tool that gives you the ability to set up a few habits and do your best to stick to them. A lot of habit apps have too many options and too many unnecessary features, then charging a stupid expensive fee to track more than one habit. I feel like this app is just right. The free version lets you track up to five habits. If you’re building new habits, that’s a pretty perfect amount. It also has a SUPER reasonably priced yearly and lifetime fee if you choose to upgrade to premium. A lot of these habit apps want to gouge you as much as possible for just tracking more than one habit. This app doesn’t do that. It seems like they really, really care about the emotional and financial well being of their users.

title: This app is a major part of my life now…

After testing them all out, I was sold on this one!!! I narrowed down my goals and the daily behaviors/actions that I wish to turn to habits. It’s been roughly two weeks and I’ve been using it everyday. I set up reminders. But, I also check on my own every morning, afternoon, and evening (before I drift off to sleep). I also look forward to going on the app to mark off my completed goals 🤗. In all, I love the app so much that using it has become a habit in itself.

title: Great design, lifetime premium, great support

The app lets you do a lot for free compared to competitors. And, best of all, the developer isn’t greedy. I get lifetime premium when I’m ready for only $6.

The design is intuitive except for not being able to drag the tracker bar backward to correct an incorrect adjustment.

Habit setup is extremely detailed and customizable. You can even pick what kind of graph you want and set a custom reminder for each habit.

Currently (but this will change soon) you can only track habits you want to make, but not any you want to break. The developer told me that they are working on this feature right now. I’m excited for an update.

Once that feature is released and I am able to test it, and love it, I’ll update my review and make 5 stars.

author: JustNtime4math

title: This app is a no brainer.
body:
First of all, I would like to say the Habit Tracker app is an app I would certainly recommend. Before I downloaded this app, I felt extremely pessimistic about what I can do to achieve a strong social life. My relationships with my relatives and my close friends were falling apart, and my mental health was placed on the back burner. But with this app, everything about this is starting to change, I feeling more confident than I had in 10 years to achieving a better future for myself, and the betterment of my well being. I’ve been through countless therapies, and doctors appointments often going out of town to meet those objectives. 

Because of this, it was an extreme drain on my mental health, not only on myself, but my parents as well, I can’t imagine how much money it costs to doing these kind of things. I say that no parent wants to go through that at all. At 14 years old, I was sent to Copper Hills in Utah for two years, this treatment program in large part did in fact help me get back on the right track, but I started to relapse into another mental breakdown this last October, and I was admitted to the hospital as a result.

I felt like that there was no hope in going back when I went through this, and I often contemplated in suicide as a result. Today, I can now see myself as a strong and capable person who can climb back up to where I left off before, and I now feel more optimistic about my bright future than I had in a long time, and with that I can now start to seeing real results, and I have my therapist, including this app to thank for the additional support.

title: Best habit tracker for iOS
body:
I used the free version of this app for about a year and it has many great features. I recently paid for the lifetime subscription because I wanted the reports and extra features. The subscriptions are affordable and very much worth it, in my opinion. I love that there are so many different ways to track habits, like daily, or 20 minutes a day, or 4 hours a week.

I recently made goals for the year and was able to start tracking every single one I wanted to in the app. My one small feature request would be to allow you to edit the frequency/time of a habit after it has been made. Like, right now, my goal may be to practice piano three times a week for 20 minutes, but if I wanted to change it to four times a week for 30 minutes next month, I would either have to change the habit and reset all my data for it or archive it and make a new one with my new goal.

Overall, though, this is an amazing app that is getting regular updates and is very well thought out. I highly recommend it if you are looking to set some goals and build new habits. I set one habit on it daily with an alarm to remind me to track my habit at the end of the day, and I have been doing so successfully for months now.
