It’s priced very reasonably and nowadays I truly appreciate a lifetime option, and not getting bogged down in recurring fees. 

The only issue I’m having with it is it doesn’t seem to sync across devices— my iPad and iPhone don’t currently match up. It’s possible the subscription only supports one device at a time, but I personally didn’t see that explicitly stated anywhere, so I’m not sure if this problem could be solved by buying premium on each device or if there’s just a bug I’m running into. title: Confusing and havent heard from support
body:
They asked me for feedback as soon as I opened the app so I’m wondering if most of the reviews here aren’t really based on what happens after you use it for a week.

What has happened for me is it doesn’t reset my weekly goals. And I can’t tell what it thinks 1 week is. There are no instructions on how to set weekly goals and the only way I can see that would do that is when you create the goal. You’d think it would reset your per-week count every seven days but it doesn’t. 

The units of count also don’t make sense. What does “count” mean? I don’t know if the units are just for my own use or if they actually change the behavior of the tracking. 

I’m mega bummed because I wanted to reinstall Done, but Done seems to be done ): .
This is a much more complicated version of Done with lots of unecessary features that don’t work in a logical way.

Another issue is when I try to swipe to log that I completed my habit for the day, it almost always fills out every single rep I meant to do for the whole week. So whenever I finish something, instead of simply ticking it off on the main screen, I have to add three extra clicks to navigate me to the tracker screen, press the plus button, then navigate back out to the main list screen again. That’s six clicks if you add the memo prompt like I did. 

Anyways I hope tech support gets back to me. I tried reaching out through the app and they said they would email me but its been a few days and nothing. I really want/ kinda NEED this thing to work. Habit trackers are the only thing that have kept me honest with my physical therapy to help me recover from an old extreme car accident. 

I used to pay a subscription for Done because it was so simple and therefore useful. I would pay a subscription if this bloated knockoff version of it actually worked and didn’t just make me confused about how many reps I’ve actually completed that week.

title: Checks all the boxes
body: This app is the perfect habit tracker for me! It has the ability to repeat daily, weekly and monthly. You can track each goal with specific units (ex. count, minutes, seconds, miles, etc.). You can also put on the timer for for the goals you’re tracking with time units or just manually enter the units. Set multiple reminders. Choose an end date (or no end date) for goals. Choose frequency. You can also set a habit with no specific day but multiple (or once) a week. Great for me because some habits I want to maintain don’t have designated days (yet). You can even set a passcode for the app. Multiple widgets. Looks clean. Clean interface. BIG PLUS: Ability to retrospectively track habits. Some days you may forget to log habits or for me, some of my habits are technically done the next day but I want it to count the previous day (I’m a night owl). Example: one of my habits is to take my nightly vitamins. I usually take them after 11:59pm but I still want it to count for that day. So this was big for me. This app really helps me be consistent with my goals. The streak 🔥 encourages me not to break my streaks, therefore my habits. BIG PLUS: ONE TIME FEE ($5.99) I don’t know why some other habit tracker apps would charge a monthly subscription fee. Ridiculous. SUGGESTIONS TO DEVELOPERS: The hidden habits don’t stay hidden. You have to manually hide them daily which is inconvenient and defeats the purpose.   Also maybe tracking items before making it a goal would be nice, so that it doesn’t affect your analytics. For instance, I just want to track my water intake before making it a goal to drink x amount a day. It would also be nice if habits could be broken down by anytime, day, night without clicking just one in “Status”. If I were to click “Now” I may not remember to change it back later but if it had sections on the normal screen, that would be cool and still keep the completed task at the bottom.

title: Lovely
body:
The design of this takes a little bit to learn but after that learning period, there’s so much usability for the day to day person. Even underneath the free umbrella, there’s a lot that can be useful. I love the simplicity of this app and it’s quiet aesthetically pleasing for me personally. You can set reminders and memos about habits each day. I’ve been using it for a few days. I’ve tried other apps like Habitica which was another great app. However, I wanted something that was less reward based and more for the sake of tracking/researching my own habits. This app stuck out among the plethora of apps on the store. I am grateful so far to have gotten it. I will probably purchase the lifetime access so I can see the weekly, monthly, and yearly diagrams from my habits. But it’s not necessary if you are just looking for something to help you keep track of your everyday habits (whether they are good or bad ones). I would recommend at least giving it a try for a period of time and seeing if you like it like I do :)

Edit: I have a suggestion for the app! They should add an option for “bad habits” that you want to stop doing. I realized I needed yo reword my bad habits in a way that I can cross them off my list. But maybe if they implemented a way for them to be in the system so it doesn’t take away from your completion rate for the day… for example, if I’m trying to quit drinking coffee, I would put “not drink coffee” as my habit. Instead of “coffee” which means the habit wouldn’t be completed and looks like you didn’t finish everything on your list (even tho that’s a good thing.) other than that, the app is great 😃

title: This app changed my life.
body: I’ve always been scatter-brained, unable to focus on a single task. I decided to make a change and get this app to help track what I’d do throughout the day. Lemme tell you, it’s so worth it to buy the premium for $5. It’s a one-time-payment so you don’t have to worry of any surcharges. I went from 2-3 habits a day at the beginning of the year, and 7 months later I’m up to around 20 habits a day. It’s okay if you don’t finish them all, because if you slowly build up a routine, and you do 5/10 habits, you still did 5 habits you wouldn’t have done otherwise. Be consistent and you’ll get the most out of this app. The UI is pleasing to the eye and customizable, which is also an added bonus. I usually never leave reviews, but after having such a positive impact in my life, I couldn’t help but write one. Get this app and buy the one-time purchase, it’ll literally change your life you’re consistent.

title: Awesome!
body: I was looking for an automated custom task tracker and this is definitely the best. I’m able to customize things on a more granular level than other apps I’ve tried. I have all my workouts, health, and learning broken down by the precise metrics as well as custom reminders that make everything work flawlessly. The UI is also great, which allows for a satisfying user experience. Another cool feature is that you can add friends to help you stay accountable. Lastly, the seamless health app integration allows for some tasks (habits) to be automatically updated with calorie count or time durations with multiple exercises available. The Apple Watch pairs great with this feature. There a very few areas that I’d change other than a few minor bugs, but I imagine they are on the devs’ radar. All-in-all, great app.

body: I really enjoyed this app because it kept me organized and it was actually very exciting to use. title: Wonderful app but could be better!
body:
This is a great app when used consistently, but for someone who already has trouble forming habits and needs the assistance of an app that is difficult! That is why even minor issues with user experience can lead to a rapid decline in usage. There are so many things this app does right, miles above any other app that I’ve used, so I’ll focus on what it does wrong for the sake of brevity:

- The option for push notifications is fantastic! Great reminder! However, if I click on the APP and not the NOTIFICATION, and mark a task as complete, the notification still persists. This tends to A) make me ignore the notifications entirely, or B) accidentally delete notifications for tasks I haven’t done, while swiping to delete notifications for tasks I have done.

- The option to skip a task is great, and the fact that it still closes the ring for the day is a solid win! This encourages me to come back to the app even if I don’t complete a task. However, it would be nice if there was also a “Reschedule” option; e.g. I have a habit reminder to do laundry every Saturday but sometimes I don’t get to it until Sunday. My options see either: A) skip the task, and not track that it was completed, or B) ignore it until it’s done on Sunday and then go back and mark Saturday as complete (possibly even adding a memo that it was done another day) but this incorrectly tracks it as being done saturday

- Widgets! I wish there was the option to just check a task off on the widget instead of clicking the widget to open the app! What’s the point of all these different widget options if they’re all just informational and not interactive, corporate says it’s the same picture!

Overall the devs have clearly worked really hard on this app and it shows. Great features and infinite customizability. I just wish these few quality improvements were made the the UX because even though they’re minor changes they can make a WORLD of difference for someone with attention deficit and difficulty forming habits.

title: really good!
body:
apologies for spelling and grammatical errors

first off, this is one of the only apps that allowed me to add enough tasks to be useful to me without paying. honestly Id think about supporting this app just because of that, but down to the actual functions

easy to use 9/10
its vary clear what you need to do but some functions could be placed better

habits to track 10/10
the app suggest habits to add which is nice, and when making your own habits you get lots of FREE and cute emoicons to add next to the action. all it takes to mark down that you completed the habit is a button and a number keypad if that habit can be done multiple times. 

notifications 10/10
I personally HATE notifications but the app does give lots of options on notifications, when to send them, what habits for, etc. you can also just completly turn them off which I loveeeee

visuals 10/10
the app is just super clean and its not overwhelming by any means, you can customize your habit colors too, if you want an even cleaner look

data summary 8/10
being completely honest, I barely look at this feature but Im sure its useful for some people. it seems convenient being able to see how many times you completed a task over a certain amount of time, and the canender seems easy to use. 

Im not sure who the developers are of this app, but props to them.

title: The format is working for me so far
body:
I have gone through multiple apps trying to find one that feels just right as Goldilocks would say. I like the chore apps but found them to be too precise. I needed something to keep track of my natural habits so I could study them more accurately. Being a super visual person the graphs work more seamlessly with how my brain works.  The notifications feel more like reminders rather than shaming me for not meeting the routine I set up. I love the option to choose my own colored tabs and symbols to personalize and identify more effectively to my own unique triggers. I love the simplicity of this app. I like the ability to change the quantity of the habit to various units. I was a bit frustrated by the units of time when a timer started and couldn’t check it off unless I went to the end of the timer. I like the possibilities of this feature. I would like an option to be able to check it off without the forced use of the timer. The notifications throughout the day remind me of what I would like to get done. I check in with this app at the end of the day to check in with all that I have done.  The first habit I want to create is understanding and improving my current habits by documenting them on a regular basis. When that is second nature I will start fine tuning the details including more accurate units of time. I would like to see sub categories I could check off. For example, 1 hour of cleaning the kitchen has sub tasks: dishes, mopping, clean the fridge, clean stove, microwave, etc. I figured out a way to track them by putting them in the notes. Unfortunately, they do not get their own graph. I could put them as a separate habit and add the category kitchen. If I did it now seeing all the tons of tasks might feel overwhelming while I am just starting out. Either way, I have figured out how to make it work for me so it is only a minor suggestion rather than a major complaint.  

Overall, I am enjoying this app. Thank you.

title: Literally only one problem, perfect otherwise!
body:
This app has been so helpful when it comes to tracking my habits and my effort to get better at doing things in a routine. My only complaint is that the notifications are very inconsistent. Sometimes they’ll work, like I get a notification for one habit, but other times they won’t. 

I have three notifications in total, one for 2:00 PM, one for 7:00 PM, and one for 10:25 PM. Without fail, the ones at 2 and 7 never go off, but the one at 10:25 does, and it’s really frustrating because no matter how many times I delete the notification and add a different time, I never get the reminder. 

It’s really a bummer because I really rely on those reminders, but I haven’t found another app as good as Habit. I’m hoping that the reminders can be fixed, as it seems I’m often contacting support about it and most of the bug updates are for it. 

Nevertheless, I am grateful for this app, and thank you to the team for all the work you put behind this!

title: Simply Amazing
body:
The simplicity and beauty of this app is much more than surface deep.  It functions as though somebody had already encountered the terrain of daily needs and set up the perfect companion app for organizing things.  I really like how the calendars look.  They display individual calendars for each habit.  This app has a ton of really good visual cues!

I think Batman himself would enjoy this app! It has a memo log for everything, great insight statistics that aren’t over bearing and provides you with enough customization to keep your habits from looking identical.

I like how each habit has its own custom alert to remind you throughout the day.  Maybe a quote or some reason that motivates you!  Each habit is different so seeing unique reminders really goes a long way. 

I like how the art is hand drawn and has the feel of a log book.  That makes me feel at home with this app.  I know good craftsmanship when I see it.  This is it!  Anybody can design an app but it takes real skill and CARE to design an app that covers all the pain points of habit builders.

I give this app 100 stars 🤩.  Thank you for creating this app!  All who were involved in the process really did an awesome job!  Premium member for life now.

title: Behavior Reduction
body: I wish there was a way to make goals to reduce behaviors! You can still largely use the features of the app to track the habit, but the "goal" presentation looks weird when it's a habit you actually want to decrease, like smoking or drinking or something. The app makes you pick values for habits that "go up"  - for example, you can not set a habit to zero. A different idea is to focus more on "going down" would be like if you had a limit of 3x opportunities throughout the day and each time you engage in the habit, you slide (left) one away from the limit you set. That, or like you get a warning or motivational message or something when you've used up all your opportunities if swiping right to count them. Ultimately, the biggest thing would be that it wouldn't still count as a streak if you went over the goal value you set for the habit.

title: Elegant yet robust habit tracking
body:
VERY CUSTOMIZABLE
What I was looking for was a habit tracking app that was simple to use, but let me customize colors and sounds. (If I get into a slump, changing up the colors and sounds helps me shake out of it.) This app does EXACTLY that. You choose literally any color, with both presets and custom color picker. Your reminder notification sound can be one of the built-ins, or you can record or upload a custom sound.

FREE VS. PAID

As is the case with most habit trackers, the app limits the number of habits you can track in the free version. A one time payment is ideal, but I understand that can be an unsustainable model for app development. At the time of my writing, there was a lifetime deal which barely exceeded the yearly option, so I bought without hesitation.

What I appreciated about the paid/premium version is that you are automatically enrolled in a 7 day free trial. While this might lead users to be disappointed if they don't realize the limitations of the free app, it beats the behavior of some other habit tracking apps that I tried (grubbing for money literally the moment you start using the app, before you even know if it meets your needs or not).

HAS WIDGETS
It comes with homescreen widgets, a nice variety of them too.

NEAT UI
I like that it offers dark and light themes, a variety of colors, and different styles for displaying your current habit statuses. I very much appreciate that system fonts are used rather than a wacky non-standard font.

Some improvements could be made to the UI– some font sizes are too small (example: Theme settings for habit bar size) and padding is sparse, leading to very small tappable areas. Keeping fonts at a legible minimum size and padding a tad more generous and consistent would be better.

MINOR NOTES
I am a bit baffled by the feature that is ever-present in the top right-hand corner, with the envelope and the tree. Why it it there? Why is it a picture of a tree? It enables you to generate and share a photo of your currently accomplished habits along with the date. I mean, it does sound pretty self explanatory, and I can see how it might lead to some nice word of mouth marketing, but I can't imagine it's important enough to permanantly occupy such a prominent position. In fact, everything above the habits portion of the screen is really not important to me: I'd prefer to see more habits vs. the meta info like the filter dropdown, the extraneous "Today" heading, and the photo sharing button.

OVERALL
Best habit tracking app for simplicity and customizability!

I will be cancelling Better Me b/c this can cover that.  I still will keep myfitnesspal b/c of the food, weight, and image tracking.

Strongly recommend this app.

title: Super Glitchy
body:
**Update**
I am so sad. I don’t think I can do this anymore. The app freezes when I try to mark certain tasks as done (not all, just very specific ones), it also decided to mark some tasks as completed on days they were not. 

This app is gorgeous and everything I wanted in a habit tracker, except for the glitches. 

******

I’m going to keep using the app, because it’s the nicest I’ve found, and works with the apple watch, but it is SUPER glitchy. 

If I set a goal, work on it for a week, then change it - for example, “walk 3x a week”, then change it to “walk Mon, Wed, Friday”, the app crashes and no longer loads. It just sits on the load screen. Even turning my phone off and on again doesn’t fix it. I can still access my goals on my watch, except for the one I just updated that crashed the app. 

So, from here on out, if I happen to need to change a goal, I will just create a new one with the new perimeters, and add in past goals met. It will be time consuming. But I haven’t found a habit tracker I like as much that works just as well with the apple watch.

title: The most intuitive and lovely habit app
body: I’ve never written a review before, and I rarely find apps I like enough to buy the premium version, but I bought this one within the first few days of using it and am so glad I did. It’s highly customizable but easy to understand, and the interface is beautiful. The scheduling and frequency targets are more flexible and more clearly explained than in any other app I’ve tried. Habits are easily grouped with tags and each one can be given a custom unit name. Now that home screen widgets have been added, I love it even more! The only things I’d like to see added in the future are the ability to export data to CSV and the option to create negative habits (e.g. for calorie tracking—I’d like to be able to hit my target by staying under a certain number rather than exceeding it.) The developer does a great job at keeping the app updated & consistently improving it, so maybe those options will be added in the future, but I’m still very satisfied overall.

title: Needs Work. Only good for daily habits.
body:
-The “all habits” calendar does not display any data. If you choose a X/week habit goal, the calendar tab does not display which days you actually did your weekly habit. Instead, it displays a circle bar on every single day of the week towards that goal. You have to individually tap on each day to check if you even did the habit on that day. 

A more intuitive way would be to simply mark every day you did your habit, perhaps with a number indicating how many times that day. 

-The home screen also appears to be broken. When you select a previous day of the week, none of your existing habits will show up. 

The only thing this app does is count your habits and computes some statistics. And even then it is clunky at marking when you did them. Selecting “1/5” for instance, then hitting the check mark... You would think this would add 1 to your habit goal, but instead it completes the entire week worth of habits in one day.

title: I love this app
body:
I love this app.  It’s pretty well laid out - fairly simple - and I love the color options. 

I love the little habit trackers inside - the colors are wonderful and it’s a nice way to see your habits aside from the list view on the main page.  I actually love that you can save a copy as a photo, print them, or send them to someone.  I kept wanting to use a habit tracker but I am way too lazy to sit and draw it out on paper and color it in or use stickers.  This app is amazing for tallying them up for you as you complete habits.  Brilliant.  

I paid for the premium feature (one time payment) and I like the additional features you get like the yearly habit tracker and I can add more than 3 habits.  It’s a reasonable price for a well designed app and it isn’t a subscription which I hate so I am willing to support that! Thank you so much for allowing us a 1x payment.  

I highly recommend this app.  It’s wonderful! 

A couple tiny things that would be nice but don’t ruin the experience or make the app bad:

1. I would love if we could change the background to something other than white or black.  White is too bright and black is too dark.  I wish there was a medium-gray type option maybe?   Something easy on the eyes that isn’t the extreme black/white would be nice.  Super minor feature though.  

2. On the main page (maybe this exists and I haven’t figured it out yet) - I would like the habits to remain in the place I have them instead of jumping to the bottom when completed.  I have them lined up in a color pattern I like and in order of importance for me. 

When they jump around after being completed when I have tons of habits - it just throws me off a little.  Super minor but would be nice to allow the option to leave them in the order you list them in the habit manager (preferred) or jump to the bottom of the screen when completed.  

3.  I kind of wish there was an option to have “bars/chunks/squares” within the color areas of a habit to show how many “counts” you have completed.  I know it has a number 2 when you’ve completed “2 of 8”, for example, but it would maybe be nice to visually see the counts in the colors.  I dunno if this would be a useful feature - maybe it wouldn’t look nice.  I kept looking for an option to show that before I realized the number was at the end of the bar indicating 2 counts.

title: Most robust habit tracking app bar none
body:
Ok, call me crazy as there’s a couple big boys out there (starts with an S and ends with an S) but if you don’t want to pay a fortune for a really full featured habit tracker, look no further. Seriously!! I didn’t get paid to say any of this. This is a really solid and full featured habit tracker. I should know I have tried well over 50 different ones and this is not my go to habit app. Why? 
1. Tags (love them!)
2. Health kit integration (why enter things twice) 
3. Well laid out 
4. Weekly means weekly, not daily. (Use it and you’ll see what I mean. One 2 other apps get this. Great job to the developer!) 
5. iCloud sync. (Hello! Why doesn’t everyone have this in their app.)
6. Vacation mode (you don’t want it, don’t use it, but nice to have!) 
7. Archive habits. Yes!!! 
8. Timers / counters built into the habits. Easy to know how long or many times you did something. 
9. Partial credit. (Nice to have to know that you maybe didn’t achieve your habit but you put in some effort.) 

And much, much more! Give it a try!

title: I Can Finally Stick To My Habits
body: I tried a lot of things to reform my goals, but this is by far the most successful. As long you don't overload yourself with an unreasonable amount of habits you should be fine. I add a new habit to the list ~every 2 weeks.
author: Amelie Bright

title: Best habit app out there
body: I've tried many, and none do add much as this one in a free, simple way. Just try it out, I'm excited to form good habits and lose the bad ones with the help of this app :)
author: Olivia Morrisoni

title: Excelent
body: ! What i love about this app is the alarming. This is what I use it for the most. Everything else is very nice also. Although something like "done" is missing, so that the alarming stops when you are done with the action for today (please tell me if I missed this option).
author: Aidan Martel

title: Intuitive, simple to use and effective.
body: Love it! Still in a trial period (I have only been using it for a couple of months) but I am seriously considering buying the pro version, not necessarily because I need it, but simply because I want to support the developers!
author: Luke Pamphlett

title: I LOVE this app.
body: The chain-method really keeps my momentum up! Habit Bull makes it so easy to manage via its wonderful interface. This app is also much better than others on the market. Thanks so much.
author: Leconfas

title: Use this now!
body: If you you want to rid yourself of a habit, or train yourself to acquire one, then use this app! Inspirational pictures on the main page encourage you to keep going, a simplistic calendar tracks your progress, so you can see how far you've come. Using this daily and it's definitely helped.
author: Declan Froggatt

title: Best in this category.
body: Gives flexible recurrence settings and any other feature I was looking for for free. Bought premium just to support devs and track way more habits. Widgets do save time.
author: Bianca Winston

title: Streamlined and effective
body: This is a great app. A clean, elegant, and easy habit tracker, which has been fun to use. I definitely recommend it! (You can only track about 5 habits until you pay a very small fee for unlimited use - totally worthwhile.)
author: Nathan Hirsch

title: Awesome interface
body: Perfect usability and does everything I want. Great for developing skills or kicking bad habits... Both of which I could use some help with.
author: Georgia Donaghy

title: Useful App
body: Really helped me to realize the focus and discipline and dedication it takes to accomplish goals, and create habits which become a part of your life. This app has helped me change my life. It shows me percentages of how i am doing and it's fun like your own personal video game but its about you and healthy habits. Its empowering, challenging, exciting and makes you feel proud of yourself when you do succeed. It also motivates you by keeping track of what you need to work on. Gives you a visual which is very helpful.
author: Phoebe Halloran

title: Awesome like a bull in a china store
body: Not terrifying, not costly, not bad - but you smash your goals like a bull does. Which makes this app awesome. Easy to use, cute reminders, and motivating - your goals will become habits with this app!!
author: Jesahuk

title: Highly recommend
body: Exactly what I needed to kick-start and maintain momentum. Could use a social function for sharing with an accountability partner, but otherwise flawless. Highly recommend!!!
author: Eden Ramsbotham

title: This app is great
body: I've only been using it for just over a week. However, it has already helped me stay consistent with 3 different habits I've been struggling to make for about 2 years. It's nice to see your progress lined out for you. It functions perfectly, and I highly recommend it!
author: Emma Brake

title: It helps by providing accountability
body: Having external accountability, even to a program on a smartphone, helps me to continue forming and maintaining my habits. And since I have nobody to impress or be embarassed to it keeps me honest.
author: Irtasom

title: Very helpful
body: I needed some help remembering and being motivated to do a few household chores regularly, and this app really helped! Maintaining a streak may seem like kind of a ridiculous thing to care about, but it's a great motivator.
author: Tasnumkk

title: Simple interface, easy to track
body: The simple interface makes habits easy to track. Chaining of successful days is visually appealing. I don't want to break the chain :)
author: Hecilasi

title: Best App Ever
body: This is the best app of its kind I've seen, and I've been looking for a while. It's super simple, so it doesn't feel like a chore to update it, the design is a perfect mix of style (especially the dark theme) and functionality. I recommend it to anyone who's been lookin for a way to finally make those habits last
author: Kimtehan09

title: 5 stars
body: Love this app! It's the best there is. You can write comments about your goals if you miss them - keeping you on top of your achievements.
author: Bistaked

title: Super like
body: I like the way it offers contextual calendar info with regard to a particular habit.. & I can easily track the sucess & failure days
author: Dr. Amer H.

title: Helped me quit bad habit!
body: This app helped me stop picking my nails! It was a bad habit I've had for 20 years. The only thing I changed was tracking with this app. Phenomenal and simple app!
author: Bankiters

title: Thank you
body: This app has helped me make my lifestyle better and improved my life. I try and get every day eating regular meal quantities, I exercise, take my vitamins, do full hygiene/grooming etc. This has been the first time I can actually achieve my goals of self care, and most importantly, because of this app, my mental health, confidence and happiness are all doing very well. Thank you developers and everyone involved in the app ❤
author: Victoria Mokare

title: Awesome App
body: Brilliant for tracking varying factors. Only issue is the success it gives you if you say you need to do something x times a week. However a work round is just to pick a (few) day(s) and tick it once done.
author: Thomas Beeby

title: Awesome in one word
body: As I need to do something and not to do something else, for years I searched for coach that do something practical for me. This app is just what I want and now, thanks to Habit Bull it happened.
author: Summer Luttrell

title: changed my life
body: Habify has finally given me a way to track my habits in a simple way that gives me motivation to keep going. I'm changing habits I've tried and failed at for years!
author: Lachlan Carroll

title: I'm happy with this app.
body: I like the fact that it has widgets and that the habits are very customisable. The one thing that it is missing, is a way to tell the app when you are sick or on holidays, so that it doesn't count those days as "fail" days.
author: Tobiasen_K

title: Very useful.
body: Helps to keep you on track. Very useful app. I upgraded because I wanted more objectives than provided in the basic version. Easy modify an objective or to add/delete. The app won't do it all for you but is fantastic for keeping track of your progress.
author: Zoe Degraves

title: Love it
body: Easy to use. I downloaded this for free and have 5 goals at the moment. Started as daily then went to 5 days per week. Once I have good streaks will bump them up by one day per week so I only miss once max.
author: Puzemasi

title: Great motivator
body: The visual of calendars really helped me realize how much I was slacking on daily personal goals and it helped build those habits quicker
author: Charlotte Ligertwood

title: Love It!!!
body: What can I say! It's amazing I love the reminders it really helps me a ton!! Plus I feel loved and motivation with every reminder!!! It does what it says it does!
author: Asinae_D

title: Loved it
body: This thing really works. I have been using it for the past month and I haven't missed a single day from a habit that I have set up. What's best is that when I'm about to break the habit, my brain has started to remind me: don't break the chain you moron!
author: Lucia Joren

title: Awesome App
body: I do use this to create new habits like fitness, and it works great. But I also use it for household stuff: reminding my household to do chores. I'm not being a jerk, but I exist in a house with 4 other adults, and I'm the only one with any drive or ambition, and they simply won't do chores without me telling them to. If you're in this situation, this app is your answer. (Don't tell me to motivate them, or leave them alone and they'll catch on, it doesn't work. They're happy living in filth.) I have daily and weekly reminders to nag them to do their chores. It works great. Summary: if you need things done on a recurring basis, this app is awesome.
author: Alexander Palfreyman

title: Very good!
body: Love the interface, easy to use, and the reminders are great for keeping me on track. I think I'll keep this app for a while.
author: Coberason

title: The coolest out there.
body: Of all if the other apps like this, this one is one of the best. I like that it is decently customizable, you can set alarms and add numbers to your habits without actually opening the app. I only wish it was more comprehensive when graphing. I have a habit that is "no more than..." and I haven't quite figured out if it is tracking my numbers the right way. You can go into the negative and that is confusing to me. Otherwise, I will definitely be using this app more. Please don't start charging!
author: Chithasoti

title: Very Helpful For Staying With Habits
body: I’ve found this app very helpful in assisting me to keep up my habits. It provides a very clean and beautiful interface. The app is simple but does not limit me. Even without paying for the full version I still find it immensely helpful. I have and do reccommended this app.
author: Axeustrea

title: Highly recommend
body:
I barely ever rate or review apps, but this one is worth it. It’s very clean, simple, and does exactly what it should do. I needed an extra boost to be able to follow through with habits and that’s what momentum provided. I’ve had minor problems (syncing pro version issue), but the dev was happy to email with helpful tips to fix it. If you get momentum on the phone and look at tips and tricks, they mention using the notification center widget. Honestly I use that all the time now, never even open the actual app. 
This has probably been one of the most impactful apps I own!
author: Isabelle Devanny

title: Very Adorable
body: I really ADORE this app, use it on my my phone. I track habits, not only like “waking up early” but also some behavioral things like “discussing relationships, speak only about yourself” as a good mental health practice. Highly recomended, I think it is must have tool for life nowadays!
author: Caitlyn Coungeau

title: Organized and well executed
body: This habit tracker makes it easy to set up new items to track, to mark them as being done (or undone, if you’ve made a mistake) and see what the past month has been like as far as regularity. The integration between the iOS version and the Mac version works great. I’ve never had the occurrence of marking something done on one device and finding that it wasn’t marked as done on the other. I looked at quite a few habit trackers, and this one was the easiest to setup and maintain. It has alarms that allow you to mark something as complete right from the iOS notification screen. It’s super easy and convenient to use.
author: Poppy Thornber

title: Minimal and Effective
body: Perfect app to begin incorporating new habits into your routine. The interface is minimal in the best of ways. Optional reminders to review your habits at the beginning of the day are helpful without being distracting. Well worth the small price.
author: Lauren Mackrell

title: Amazing App!!!
body: Holy. This is the first app that has ever made a difference in my life. I downloaded this app in April after being frustrated that I had gained a little weight and before this app, I was never able to go to the gym consistently for more than 4-5 weeks. Seven months later and I am still going strong thanks to this app! I recommend this app to anyone who looking to make or break a habit! Also the design is so simple and easy to use!
author: Imogen Baldessin

title: Love the simplicity
body: After purchasing and using the full version of this app, I would recommend it for anyone interested in developing habits with the help of an app. Only thing I wish is that it was optimized for iPhone X.
author: Clawdefa

title: Simple and affective
body: I wanted an interface that helped me visualise my streak; it does that. I’ve exercised everyday for a month because I don’t want the angry red square. Simple and affective. Would probably pay for the subscription once I hit the three habit limit
author: Joukyras

title: Fantastic, simple motivator
body: Momentum has a standout feature that sets it above the rest; you see all your progress straight away when opening the app. No need to navigate menus, all your streaks and wins are there. To me this is the most important feature, as setting habits requires discipline and patience, and having that clear reminder of successes makes it that much easier to create new habits.
author: Isabella To Rot

title: It works.
body: I have been looking for an app to help me consistent in my daily habits. I’m glad to say this is the one. The layout is very simple and there aren’t too many features so it keeps u focused. And seeing your streak in green makes u feel good and makes u want to keep going. I started with a small habit like taking my vitamins and now after 5 months i don’t even need a reminder. For people who are just looking for a simple app that is efficient, I would definitely recommend this.
author: Viviane Torp

title: Really good!
body: It would be great if you could set colors on completing different habits. To differentiate between good and bad habits. And add weekly summary. Otherwise great concept!
author: Araceli Carroll

title: Love this app
body: Simple and easy to use. Great minimalist design, no fuss! I love that we get to support the developer's work without having to pay a monthly fee but a one-time fee. Or if you don't need, the "free" 3 habits work really well too. Great design and solution overall! Keep it up.
author: Rebecca McGee

title: Love It!
body: It’s only one day, but I can surely say I LOVE this app. It is so simple and amazing and most importantly helpful. I really like the feature that you can add notes to any particular day and it will be marked with a dot. The way the calendar is shown is also extremely helpful and motivating as you see your progression over time. I will definitely buy full version.
author: Eve Rintel
